summary.eli5: The photo you give the model.
summary.simple: The image, resized to a square and stored as 3 colour channels (red, green, blue).

summary.eli5: Looks at the picture again and again, each time seeing bigger shapes but in less detail.
summary.simple: Turns the image into feature maps. Each stride-2 step halves the width and height and adds channels, so the map holds more meaning and less pixel detail.
summary.engineer: Hierarchical feature extractor producing P3/8, P4/16 and P5/32 maps through strided convs and CSP-style blocks.

summary.eli5: Mixes what the small, detailed maps saw with what the big-picture maps understood.
summary.simple: Passes information up and down between the feature maps (top-down, then bottom-up) so every map knows about both fine details and the bigger context.
summary.engineer: PAN-FPN style multi-scale fusion: top-down upsample + concat, then bottom-up strided conv + concat.

summary.eli5: Makes the final guesses: where things are and what they are.
summary.simple: Looks at every cell of each feature map and predicts box sides and class scores (plus masks, keypoints or angles for other tasks).
summary.engineer: Decoupled per-level prediction branches (box regression, classification, task-specific outputs) on P3–P5.

summary.eli5: Cleans up the guesses before showing them to you.
summary.simple: Steps that run only when using the model: drop weak guesses and, for many versions, remove duplicate boxes with NMS.
summary.engineer: Confidence filtering, box decoding and (unless end-to-end) non-maximum suppression.

summary.eli5: How the model is graded while it learns. Not used when it is finished.
summary.simple: Parts used only during training: which predictions should match which real objects (the assigner) and how wrong they are (the losses).
summary.engineer: Label assignment and loss terms; absent from the exported inference graph.
